highlightAliases.old: Cardiac rehab: only one-third of eligible patients participate (12% in a 600k-patient Medicare cohort) (p830). highlightAliases.old: Inpatient rehab facility: at least 3 hours of therapy/day required, 24-hr nursing (p822).
highlightAliases.new: US Medicare inpatient rehabilitation includes 24-hour rehabilitation nursing and generally 3 hours of therapy per day on at least 5 days/week, or 15 hours in 7 consecutive days in documented cases. Multiple therapy disciplines participate, including PT or OT (p822; CMS inpatient rehabilitation criteria).

highlightAliases.old: PAD: walk-to-pain program needs ≥6 months for benefit (p830).
highlightAliases.new: PAD with claudication: supervised exercise uses intermittent walking to moderate-to-maximum symptoms, alternating with rest. A standard program is 30–45 minutes of active exercise at least 3 times/week for at least 12 weeks; continue training thereafter. The six-month period described on p830 is not a minimum time to benefit (2024 ACC/AHA PAD guideline).

highlightAliases.old: An inpatient rehab facility requires a minimum of 3 hours of therapy daily; a skilled nursing facility has no required intensity or duration of therapy (p822).
highlightAliases.new: A US Medicare inpatient rehabilitation facility generally provides 3 hours of therapy on at least 5 days/week, or 15 hours over 7 consecutive days in documented cases. A skilled nursing facility has no equivalent fixed session-intensity requirement (p822, CMS inpatient rehabilitation coverage criteria).
